Article Title: Cong-led oppn demands Gyanesh ouster, Supreme Court probe
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi

NEW DELHI: Congress Wednesday led the opposition in demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar be sacked and an SC-monitored probe be ordered into the "rot", amid reports that two ECs repeatedly opposed various steps taken about SIR.The opposition announced it will move "impeachment motions" against Kumar whenever a "special session" of Parliament is called. It underlined that a removal notice against Kumar, submitted in April, is pending with the Rajya Sabha chairperson. Mamata Banerjee, CPM's John Brittas, CPI(ML)'s Dipankar Bhattacharya, DMK's M K Stalin, Sena (UBT)'s Uddhav Thackeray, NCP(SP)'s Supriya Sule, CPI's D Raja, AAP and SP demanded SIR be halted.With vote chori, BJP , RSS & EC committed act of treason: Rahul Gandhi Sources said the INDIA bloc will jointly take forward the fight against CEC. LoP Rahul Gandhi said, "Vote chori is a crime against people and a direct attack on our Constitution. BJP, RSS and EC who organised it have committed act of treason. Justice will be served." Mamata said Kumar should be arrested, while TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee demanded a "look out circular" be issued against the CEC to prevent him from "fleeing".Stalin said Kumar had no right to continue in office and must resign. He sought a fair probe "into everything that transpired within EC", adding those responsible should be held accountable. Terming the reports' findings "explosive", he said it cast "serious doubts" over the results of every assembly election held after the SIR exercise.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and MP Abhishek Singhvi said the opposition has been raising questions about the fairness of elections and EC's role for a long time, but their concerns went unheeded."Misuse of Form 6, misuse of software, tampering with voter lists, decisions without transparency - these are all now in front of the country. Then what did the CEC do about these objections? In the first three phases of SIR, 13.8 crore names were removed from draft electoral rolls of 31 states and UTs."Party general secretary K C Venugopal said, "How the hell can one man, acting on his master's orders, strike off names at whim? How can he sideline fellow constitutional officers to take blatantly illegal steps that put our democracy in danger?"Singhvi said the revelations are an example of a "double bulldozer sarkar". He said while an external bulldozer works against institutions, an internal bulldozer is CEC who bulldozed his own organisation and colleagues and "hijacked" EC. He said SC has clearly ruled that all election commissioners, including the CEC, function on equal footing, and the revelations about the watchdog's functioning show that election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, who dissented against the CEC were in a majority.
Article Summary: The opposition announced it will move "impeachment motions" against Kumar whenever a "special session" of Parliament is called. A removal notice against Kumar, submitted in April, is pending with the Rajya Sabha chairperson. LoP Rahul Gandhi said, "Vote chori is a crime against people and a direct attack on our Constitution"

Article Title: 'Bihar, Maharashtra, Delhi, Haryana & West Bengal': Oppn seeks fresh polls after EC 'dissent' report
Article Text:
Opposition leaders have stepped up demands for action against the Election Commission, with calls for CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s removal, an investigation into the poll panel’s functioning and, in some states, fresh elections. Leaders have also questioned the SIR exercise and alleged irregularities in electoral-roll revisions.

Stalin and Rahul hit out at EC

Mamata Banerjee calls report ‘scandalous’

Akhilesh Yadav questions poll panel’s functioning

NEW DELHI: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav on Wednesday accused the Election Commission of being misused to benefit the BJP and alleged that election rules had been changed to weaken the Opposition’s ability to challenge poll results.At a press conference, Tejashwi questioned the functioning of the poll panel, raised concerns over changes to the retention period for voting and counting records, and demanded fresh elections in Bihar and Bengal. He also called for the removal of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“Whether it is the results in Bihar or Maharashtra, Delhi, Haryana, or Bengal—the opposition has not lost. Rather, in these states, the EC has been misused to ensure that the BJP wins,” he said.He alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah had “flouted all the rules” and claimed the CEC had acted according to their wishes.“And this process is still continuing. It is going on in several states, and it is being carried out arbitrarily. There are objections from two Election Commissioners as well. Even then, neither Modi ji nor Amit Shah ji is coming forward and saying anything about it,” he said.He also questioned the change in the period for retaining voting and counting records. He said the earlier period of up to one year had been reduced to 45 days.“That means, when there is no evidence left, what can the opposition do? When they go to court, there will be no evidence, so there will be no benefit,” he said.On the appointment of the CEC, Tejashwi said the earlier selection panel included the Chief Justice of India, while a Union minister is now part of the panel.“This means that, as Modi ji wishes, one Gyanesh ji may be removed, but the BJP can bring in another Gyanesh Kumar,” he said.He also alleged that elections in Bihar and Bengal had been illegal and demanded fresh polls in both states.Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi also hit out at the Election Commission over the alleged irregularities, calling “vote chori” a crime against Indian voters and an attack on the Constitution.“Vote chori is a crime against the Indian people and a direct attack on our constitution. The BJP, RSS and EC who organised it have committed an act of treason. Justice will be served,” he said.DMK supremo and former Tamil Nadu chief minister MK Stalin also demanded the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. He cited allegations over the functioning of the EC during the special intensive revision of electoral rolls.Stalin said the DMK and other opposition parties had opposed the deletion of voters from electoral rolls under the SIR exercise. He said the process, carried out months before elections in different states, had faced allegations of irregularities, particularly in West Bengal.He said, "The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, along with other Opposition parties, has consistently opposed the move to delete crores of voters from the electoral rolls in the name of the Special Intensive Revision (#SIR). Rushed through just months ahead of elections in State after State, the exercise was riddled with irregularities and sparked widespread unrest, particularly in West Bengal."Stalin said the reported objections by election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi over decisions related to SIR raised questions about the functioning of the three-member poll panel. Responding to a report by the Indian Express, he claimed the two commissioners had been kept unaware of key decisions and that their objections had been brushed aside on 14 occasions in 10 months."Gyanesh Kumar had been acting unilaterally and in secrecy, without the concurrence of the other two election commissioners. Even more alarming is the revelation that Thiru. Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Thiru."Stalin said the EC's decisions should follow the majority view when its members disagree. He argued that concerns raised by two serving commissioners could not be treated merely as an internal or procedural issue."Where the commissioners differ in opinion on any matter, the decision must be based on the majority view. If two of its three members were themselves kept unaware of what was being done in the commission’s name, this cannot be dismissed as a mere internal or procedural matter. It constitutes a grave assault on Indian democracy," he said.The DMK chief also raised questions over electoral-roll appeals filed even after courts had directed that certain voters be added to the rolls. He questioned who authorised and filed such appeals.Stalin said the party had earlier moved an impeachment motion against Gyanesh Kumar and demanded that he step down.“Gyanesh Kumar must go immediately. The SIR exercise must be halted,” Stalin said, while calling for a “fair and thorough investigation” into the functioning of the Election Commission.Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee also attacked the Election Commission over the reported objections by the two commissioners to decisions linked to the SIR process.Reacting to the Indian Express report, Mamata alleged that the poll panel had been misused and demanded action against Gyanesh Kumar.“This is such a scandalous story. We had never seen this in our lives. This election commissioner must be arrested. He has no moral authority to continue, and BJP must see that they cannot destroy our Constitution. They cannot demolish democracy,” she said.Mamata also alleged that people linked to the BJP had been deployed in the electoral-roll process and accused the CEC of misusing the police.“They cannot depute their own EROs in the name of BJP IT Team. What we said earlier has now been exposed,” she said.She further said, “Gyanesh Kumar has misused Police and with BJP they have deputed their own BJP-minded people. Such a scandal has never happened. If you have any honour, you yourself would ask to be arrested. You should be arrested.”Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also questioned the functioning of the Election Commission, saying the reported objections by two election commissioners had raised serious concerns over the poll panel's impartiality.Addressing a press conference in Lucknow, Akhilesh referred to reports that Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders concerning SIR and electoral-roll procedures.“This is dangerous for our democracy. This is an attempt to weaken our democracy,” he said.Akhilesh questioned whether elections held during a period when the Election Commission was allegedly not acting impartially could be considered fair.“This means that the governments which have been formed during this period are unconstitutional governments,” he said.In an earlier post on X, he described the reported objections by the two commissioners as “extremely serious news” and urged the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance of the matter.He also alleged that voters supporting the Samajwadi Party had been systematically removed from electoral rolls and claimed that no action was taken despite the party bringing the matter to the Election Commission's notice.“Samajwadi Party voters were systematically deleted from the Election Commission's voters list. We brought this to the notice of the Election Commission, but no action was taken against anyone.Rampant malpractice was committed on a massive scale in the by-elections,” he said.The EC has rejected the suggestion that its decisions were taken without the participation of all three commissioners. It said decisions, including those related to SIR, were taken unanimously with the approval of the CEC and the two other election commissioners.The poll panel said written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks were standard practices within a multi-member constitutional body. It said differing views were part of institutional deliberations before final decisions were taken and that all official orders had legal sanction and followed established procedures.
Article Summary: Opposition leaders have stepped up demands for action against the Election Commission. Calls for CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s removal, an investigation into the poll panel's functioning and fresh elections. Leaders have also questioned the SIR exercise and alleged irregularities in electoral-roll revisions.

Article Title: 'Arrest poll panel chief Gyanesh Kumar': Mamata Banerjee demands repoll in Bengal amid EC 'SIR split' row
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Wednesday demanded fresh Assembly elections in West Bengal using the pre-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list while announcing pan-India protests against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, after a report claimed two Election Commissioners had raised objections to aspects of the voter-roll revision exercise.Reacting to a media report, Mamata demanded Kumar's arrest and accused the Election Commission of working in favour of the BJP."Re-election must be held in West Bengal with the old voter list," Banerjee said during a Facebook Live, adding that there would be "pan-India protests till Gyanesh Kumar remains CEC". "It has now been proven that the BJP and the EC looted the West Bengal assembly polls," she alleged.Mamata also called for Kumar to be arrested, saying, "He must be immediately arrested and put behind bars. The chair of the CEC is not for a person like him.""This is such a scandalous story. We had never seen this in our lives. This Election Commissioner must be arrested. He has no moral authority to continue," she said, referring to the report.The TMC leader said INDIA bloc partners had discussed the issue and would meet soon.Meanwhile, in another TMC pushback, national general secretary and MP Abhishek Banerjee separately accused the election commission of deliberately deleting 30 lakh voter names from West Bengal electoral rolls to benefit the BJP.He alleged that similar manipulation had taken place in Haryana and Bihar and demanded the immediate arrest of Kumar."The allegations we raised earlier have today been echoed by the other Election Commissioners as well. Just as the names of 30 lakh people were deleted from the voter list to benefit one political party, the same was done in Haryana and Bihar," Abhishek alleged.Abhishek also questioned the process through which Kumar was appointed, citing a split Supreme Court verdict on the Election Commission selection panel and the dismissal of an impeachment motion moved by Opposition parties.The Election Commission, however, said that "operational queries or inputs" had been raised by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on matters including the SIR exercise, but maintained that these related to the draft stage and were part of "standard administrative practice aimed at safeguarding voter rights". The poll panel also said decisions relating to the SIR were taken unanimously with the approval of all three Election Commissioners.The row erupted when a media report claimed that Sandhu and Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders concerning the SIR, including some that they allegedly said were taken without their knowledge.
Article Summary: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee demanded fresh Assembly elections in West Bengal using the pre-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list. She announced pan-India protests against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The row erupted when a media report claimed two Election Commissioners had raised objections to aspects of the voter-roll revision exercise.

Article Title: Rajya Sabha polls for 12 seats: BJP likely to retain 8 in UP, SP eyes gain, BSP at risk
Article Text:
BJP likely to retain 8 UP seats, SP eyes 2, BSP faces exit

NEW DELHI: The BJP is set to have the numbers on its side in the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh, with the party-led alliance expected to win eight of the 10 seats going to polls in the state. The Samajwadi Party could take the remaining two seats, based on the current strength of parties in the assembly.The Election Commission on Tuesday announced polls for 12 Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal. Voting, if required, will be held on October 16, with the results also to be declared the same day.The BJP is also expected to add one seat to its Rajya Sabha tally by winning the lone seat from West Bengal. The seat became vacant after actor Rukmini Mallick, popularly known as Koel, resigned from the House. The Trinamool Congress had sent her to the Rajya Sabha before losing power in the assembly election held earlier this year.In Uttar Pradesh, the BJP-led alliance has around 290 MLAs, while the SP-Congress combine has about 103. A candidate needs around 37 votes to win a Rajya Sabha seat.The BJP can comfortably win seven seats, while the SP-Congress combine can secure two.The contest for the 10th seat could be closer, with the BJP-led alliance starting with around 31 votes against around 29 for the SP-Congress side.The polls could also mark the end of the BSP's representation in Parliament. Mayawati's party has no member in the Lok Sabha and its only MLA in Uttar Pradesh, Uma Shankar Singh, died in August. The term of BSP's lone Rajya Sabha member, Ramji Gautam, ends in November.Gautam is among the nine Uttar Pradesh members whose terms are ending. The others are Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri, BJP leaders Arun Singh, Geeta Shakya, Neeraj Shekhar, Brijlal, B L Verma and Seema Dwivedi, and SP leader Ram Gopal Yadav.Puri's continuation in the Union Cabinet will depend on whether the BJP nominates him for another Rajya Sabha term.The 10th Uttar Pradesh seat was held by former deputy chief minister Dinesh Sharma. It became vacant earlier this month after Sharma resigned from the Rajya Sabha following his appointment as lieutenant governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.The BSP had managed to retain its Rajya Sabha presence in 2020 after the BJP fielded only eight candidates for 10 seats. The move allowed the BSP and SP to each elect one member unopposed.Gautam was elected unopposed after the nomination of an SP-backed Independent candidate was rejected. The SP had then alleged an understanding between the BJP and BSP.In Uttarakhand, BJP Rajya Sabha member Naresh Bansal's term is ending. The BJP, which has a comfortable majority in the state assembly, is expected to retain the seat.The election notification will be issued on September 29. Candidates can file nominations till October 6. Polling and counting will take place on October 16, if required.
Article Summary: BJP likely to retain 8 UP seats, SP eyes 2, BSP faces exit. Election Commission on Tuesday announced polls for 12 Rajya Sabha seats. Voting, if required, will be held on October 16, with results also to be declared the same day.

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission has rejected reports of differences within the poll panel over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), saying all decisions related to the exercise were taken "unanimously".The poll body clarified that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi did raise concerns over some aspects of voter roll deletion and database handling, but these did not amount to disagreement with the final decisions taken by the Commission.The clarification came after an Indian Express report triggered a row by claiming that the two Election Commissioners had raised objections to the Commission's decisions 14 times over the past 10 months during the SIR exercise.EC sources told PTI that all decisions taken by the Election Commission, including those related to the SIR, were unanimous and had the approval of Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi as well as Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Responding to queries, officials said Sandhu and Joshi had flagged issues related to the deletion of names from electoral rolls in various states and the handling of voter data.Officials also pointed out that the law governing the Election Commission, as well as a Supreme Court judgment, provides that decisions should, as far as possible, be taken unanimously. Where unanimity is not possible, the majority view prevails.Meanwhile, opposition sharpened its attack on the Election Commission over the SIR, claiming it was meant to target electors not aligned to the BJP and its allies.Urging the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognizance of the issue, several opposition parties attacked Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and accused him of becoming a puppet of those in power.In a social media post, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav accused the poll panel of hatching a conspiracy to "wipe out democracy.""This is an extremely serious news that in the past 10 months, 2 Election Commissioners have registered their objections 14 times against the Election Commission's wrong decisions," Akhilesh said."This directly means that all Election Commissioners are not able to perform their rightful duties. If the members of an independent body do not have the freedom to carry out just actions or if there is no hearing of theirs, then these are extremely fatal and dangerous circumstances for democracy. For some people to betray democracy by becoming puppets of those in power is a grave constitutional crime. This is nothing less than a conspiracy to wipe out democracy," he added.Mamata Trinamool Congress (MTMC) also slammed CEC Kumar and said that the opposition should reintroduce the impeachment motion against Kumar in Parliament."Five months ago, more than 60 Rajya Sabha Members of Parliament... when only 50 were needed, wrote to the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha moving a motion to remove the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, that was five months ago. Now today, after this big news break that two Election Commissioners objected to many of the CEC's actions, it's time to bring out the Rajya Sabha motion to impeach the CEC and save democracy," MTMC's Derek O' O'Brien said.The issue is likely to escalate further as leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has been vehement in his criticism of the Election Commission and the SIR process, alleging that it has resulted in the denial of voting rights.
Article Summary: The Election Commission has rejected reports of differences within the poll panel over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) The poll body clarified that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi did raise concerns over some aspects of voter roll deletion and database handling.

NEW DELHI: Differences of opinion within EC are a sign of its democratic functioning, BJP said Wednesday as it mounted a strong counter-charge against the Opposition over its attack on the poll body and govt, saying its rivals have been trying to discredit institutions since 2014, including before the rollout of SIR, due to their dwindling popular support."If there is no discussion of any kind among three election commissioners and they simply agree to everything, then these very opposition parties will call it dictatorship and claim that they were all 'yes men' because they were appointed by govt," BJP's Sambit Patra said.Now, the media has reported their correspondences as a divergence of views on the appropriateness of some measures taken by the commission, and this is a sign of a healthy democracy, he added.Targeting the Opposition for its allegation that BJP's impressive run of recent poll victories was aided by SIR, he said, "The statistics from Bengal expose the Opposition's narrative of 'vote chori', as TMC won 13 of the 20 seats with the highest number of deleted voters, while BJP won only six." Article Title: Nandigram bypoll: Congress candidate Milan Pradhan sent to judicial custody till October 7
Article Text:
Congress' Milan Pradhan (File photo)

Congress moves Calcutta HC against Pradhan's arrest

NEW DELHI: A court in West Bengal's Purba Medinipur district on Wednesday sent Milan Pradhan, the Congress ' candidate for the upcoming Nandigram bypoll, to judicial custody until October 7, a day after voting, in connection with a 2007 criminal case.The Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate of Contai Court remanded Pradhan to judicial custody after the prosecution sought his custody in connection with a murder charge.Pradhan, who was already in judicial custody until October 5 in a separate Arms Act case, was arraigned on murder and other charges in connection with a case also registered in 2007 during the Nandigram anti-land acquisition movement, his lawyer, Prasenjit Jana, said.The court rejected the Congress candidate's bail plea, Jana added.The order effectively ended Pradhan's chances of campaigning for the byelection, as campaigning is scheduled to conclude on October 4. The counting of votes will be held on October 9.Earlier in the day, the Congress said it had moved the Calcutta high court seeking bail for Pradhan. The high court agreed to hear the matter on Thursday. The West Bengal government did not mention this case during a hearing on September 22.Pradhan's advocate, Ayan Bhattacharjee, mentioned the matter before Justice Sauagata Bhattacharyya, submitting that the Congress candidate had been shown as arrested and produced before the court for remand in the case.Justice Bhattacharyya on Tuesday verbally asked the West Bengal government's counsel to allow Pradhan to contest the Nandigram byelection, provided he gets bail in the five criminal cases in which he has been arrested.Pradhan's arrest on September 18 came just hours after Mamata Banerjee announced that her faction of the Trinamool Congress would support the Congress candidate in Nandigram, after its nominee, Sanchita Pradhan De, withdrew from the contest.The following day, he was sent to judicial custody by the Haldia sub-divisional court until October 3 in connection with four other pending non-bailable arrest warrants linked to cases in Nandigram dating back to 2007.Several criminal cases were registered against Pradhan in 2007 at police stations in Nandigram and Khejuri in Purba Medinipur district.During a hearing on an application filed by him seeking protection from coercive action in six other cases registered against him, the state on Tuesday informed the High Court that five of them had been withdrawn by the previous government and that he was not wanted in the sixth case.The high court was informed on Tuesday that Pradhan had been arrested and sent to judicial remand in connection with the other five criminal cases.The October 6 bypoll to the Nandigram Assembly seat was necessitated after chief minister Suvendu Adhikari vacated the constituency and retained Mamata Banerjee's erstwhile stronghold of Bhabanipur. He won both seats in the assembly polls held earlier this year. The BJP won the assembly elections to form its first government in the state, while the TMC was voted out after 15 years.
Article Summary: Pradhan was already in judicial custody until October 5 in a separate Arms Act case. He was arraigned on murder and other charges in connection with a case also registered in 2007 during the Nandigram anti-land acquisition movement. The court rejected the Congress candidate's bail plea.

Article Title: 'Judges appoint judges' is a myth: SC split over CEC appointment law, differences over Constitution Bench referral
Article Text:
Supreme Court

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the Chief Justice of India be included in the selection panel for Chief Election Commissioner? Yes, definitely. No, it is not necessary. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday delivered a split verdict on whether the challenge to the law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners should be considered by a Constitution Bench.Under the law, the selection panel comprises the Prime Minister, a Union cabinet minister and the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha.Justice Dipankar Datta countered the Centre's argument against the collegium system for appointing judges, saying the perception that "judges appoint judges" is a myth.Justice Datta also said that there was no need to refer the case to the constitution bench and a two-judge bench can examine its validity.Last month, underscoring the need for an independent and impartial process for selection of the chief election commissioner and election commissioners, Supreme Court said Election Commission must not only act independently but must also be seen to act independently. The court questioned why Parliament, while framing the law, decided not to include Chief Justice of India in the selection panel.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma said the CJI was part of selection panels for CBI director and Lokpal, and asked what could be the reason for excluding him from the process of selecting CEC and ECs — posts that are among the most important for a democracy.The court reserved its verdict on the Centre’s plea that the matter be referred to a constitution bench.The court is hearing challenges to the constitutional validity of the 2023 Act, under which CEC and ECs are appointed by President on the recommendation of a selection committee consisting of PM, leader of the opposition, and a Union Cabinet minister nominated by PM. SG Tushar Mehta argued that the court could not begin with an assumption that the PM would act against democratic principles.
Article Summary: The court is hearing challenges to the constitutional validity of the 2023 Act. The court questioned why Parliament, while framing the law, decided not to include Chief Justice of India in the selection panel. Justice Dipankar Datta countered the Centre's argument against the collegium system for appointing judges.

Article Title: 9 dead after moving bus catches fire on Yamuna Expressway near Noida airport
Article Text:
A passenger bus caught fire on the Yamuna Expressway





NOIDA: Nine passengers were killed after a private bus travelling from Delhi to Mahoba caught fire on the Yamuna Expressway near Jewar late Wednesday night.Several other passengers sustained burn injuries and were rushed to Kailash Hospital in Jewar, officials said.The incident occurred around 11.30pm near kilometre 33 of the Yamuna Expressway, when the bus, operated by Raj Kalpana Travels, was travelling from Delhi towards Agra. The complainant, Sunil Kumar, a resident of Hamirpur, told police that around 30-35 passengers were travelling in the bus.According to the complaint, passengers began noticing a burning smell coming from the driver's cabin. They allegedly informed the driver and conductor about it, but the two did not stop the bus or inspect the suspected source of the smell. The complaint further alleged that the driver and conductor continued smoking inside the cabin and dismissed the passengers' concerns, saying that such a smell was common in the bus.A short while later, flames suddenly erupted near the driver's seat and rapidly spread through the vehicle. Passengers raised an alarm and repeatedly asked the driver to stop the bus, but the driver allegedly failed to act immediately.As the fire intensified, smoke filled the passenger compartment, leaving several people trapped inside. Sunil and some other passengers managed to escape by jumping out of the bus after it stopped. Several others, however, were unable to get out because of the flames and thick smoke.The injured passengers were taken to Kailash Hospital in Jewar for treatment. On reaching the hospital, the complainant was informed that doctors had declared nine people dead.The complaint also stated that passengers' bags, mobile phones and other belongings were destroyed in the fire. Luggage kept in the bus's luggage compartment and on its roof was also burnt.Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh each from the PM National Relief Fund for the next of kin of the nine deceased and Rs 50,000 for each injured person.Expressing grief over the incident, Modi said he was "distressed" by the loss of lives and prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured.President Droupadi Murmu also expressed grief over the deaths and extended condolences to the families of the victims. Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath had earlier announced financial assistance of Rs 2 lakh each for the families of the deceased and Rs 50,000 each for the injured.Police have registered a case based on the complaint and initiated an investigation. The identities of the deceased and the exact cause of the fire are yet to be officially ascertained. Police are also expected to examine the bus, statements of survivors and other evidence to determine how the fire started and whether safety precautions were ignored.
Article Summary: The incident occurred around 11.30pm near kilometre 33 of the Yamuna Expressway. The bus, operated by Raj Kalpana Travels, was travelling from Delhi towards Agra. Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh each from the PM National Relief Fund for the next of kin.

Article Title: ‘Tried to pull me into SUV’: DU student alleges eve-teasing by group in Delhi; FIR filed
Article Text:
During the enquiry, police traced the vehicle allegedly involved in the incident. (Image Social Media)

(With Agency Inputs)





NEW DELHI: A Delhi University student was allegedly harassed by a group of men travelling in a car in northwest Delhi's Mukherjee Nagar area, following which police registered a case on Thursday.The incident took place around 9:30 pm on Wednesday when Delhi University student Naman was driving the car. He was accompanied by two to three other persons when the alleged offence took place."Police launched an inquiry based on the complaint and traced the car allegedly used in the incident," Deputy Commissioner of Police (Northwest) Akansha Yadav said.An FIR has been registered at Mukherjee Nagar police station under sections 78 (Stalking), 79 (Word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman) and 3(5) (Common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).On the basis of a complaint from a woman student in Mukherjee Nagar that an SUV driver tried to pull her into the vehicle after he passed comments at her, the police have registered a case and are investigating the matter, said Delhi Police.
Article Summary: A Delhi University student was allegedly harassed by a group of men travelling in a car in northwest Delhi's Mukherjee Nagar area. The incident took place around 9:30 pm on Wednesday. Police launched an inquiry based on the complaint and traced the car.

Article Title: Gym complaints, obscene videos, deleted data: Inside cops probe into Delhi park gang-rape accused
Article Text:
Delhi Police are investigating the alleged gangrape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park





NEW DELHI: An earlier episode involving complaints against one of the accused at a gym and the recovery of several obscene videos from another accused’s phone have emerged as part of the Delhi Police investigation into the alleged gangrape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park.Police said Hemant, one of the three accused, was removed from a gym he frequented about a month ago after its management allegedly received several complaints from women about his behaviour.A senior police officer said investigators are examining the complaints and checking whether the episode has any connection with the present case.The investigation has also revealed that several “objectionable” videos were allegedly found on the mobile phone of accused Asif. Police have sent the phones of all three accused to the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) to examine their digital activity.Investigators are checking whether any video of the 17-year-old victim was recorded and are also attempting to retrieve data allegedly deleted from the phones of Hemant and his brother Mukesh.Police are examining the accused's search history, contacts, call records and other digital evidence to reconstruct their activities before and after Monday evening’s alleged assault.The police are also investigating whether the three men had been involved in any similar incidents earlier. According to investigators, the accused frequently visited Aastha Kunj Park and are being questioned about their movements and activities there.So far, police said they have not found any formal complaint against the trio relating to an earlier incident. Investigators are checking whether any potential victims may have refrained from approaching police.The three accused have been arrested and sent to judicial custody. Police are continuing their probe into the alleged assault as well as the digital evidence recovered from their phones.
Article Summary: Delhi Police are investigating the alleged gangrape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park. Police have sent the phones of all three accused to the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) to examine their digital activity.

Article Title: Uddhav should stop blaming ECI for his defeats: CM
Article Text:
CM Devendra Fadnavis

Kolhapur:





Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray should stop blaming Election Commission of India (ECI) ECI for his defeats and Mahayuti’s win in Maharashtra , chief minister Devendra Fadnavis said on Wednesday while speaking in Solapur.Asked about Thackeray’s demand for re-elections in Maharashtra and other states over ECI row, Fadnavis called it futile, citing the idiom: “The wound is on the forehead, but the bandage is tied to the knee”.“Why did he lose, why did people reject him? Instead of researching this, he only does one thing, that is, blaming the ECI. If Congress wins Telangana then ECI is doing a good job; if Congress wins Karnataka then ECI is good. But it is bad when Mahayuti wins in Maharashtra. This should stop,” Fadnavis said while speaking to the reporters in Solapur during a field visit to gauge the crop loss situation amid severe water scarcity.Addressing a news conference on Wednesday, Thackeray demanded sacking of chief election commissioner Dyanesh Kumar over alleged objections by the other two election commissioners.Lakhs of voters were added post-Lok Sabha election in Maharashtra suspiciously for the assembly election, which, according to him, led to Maha Vikas Aghadi’s defeat.The ECI, however, has denied the allegations. Thackeray said that Kumar’s conduct should also be probed.
Article Summary: Uddhav Thackeray should stop blaming Election Commission of India (ECI) ECI for his defeats and Mahayuti’s win in Maharashtra, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis said on Wednesday. “Why did he lose, why did people reject him? Instead of researching this, he only does one thing, that is, blaming the ECI. This should stop,” he said.

Article Title: Mahayuti allies spar over two seats in Pune division as MLC polls for graduates and teachers' constituencies announced
Article Text:
The voting will be held on Oct 23, with counting and results on Oct 27

Kolhapur:





Political activity in Pune division has gathered momentum with Election Commission on Tuesday announcing biennial elections to Maharashtra Legislative Council from graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies. The voting will be held on Oct 23, with counting and results on Oct 27.The Pune division constituency — covering Pune, Satara, Solapur, Sangli, and Kolhapur districts — will elect one representative each from the graduates and teachers’ constituencies to the legislative council. Even before the formal election process began, political activity in Pune division had intensified, particularly within Mahayuti, where BJP Shiv Sena and NCP have staked a claim to the two seats.BJP has asserted its traditional hold over both the constituencies, pointing out that it won the seats repeatedly in the past. Senior BJP member and minister Chandrakant Patil, a two-time MLC from the graduates’ constituency, has already begun projecting Vivekanand College chief executive officer Kaustubh Gawade as a likely face for the teachers’ constituency and Kranti Sugar Factory chairperson Sharad Lad for the graduates’ constituency at public gatherings.Alliance partner Shiv Sena has also thrown its hat into the ring by declaring deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde’s close aide Mangesh Chivate as its aspirant for the teachers’ constituency. The party has also floated Eknath Swabhimani Shikshak Sanghatana and stepped up outreach efforts through meetings and gatherings of teachers across the division.NCP, meanwhile, has staked a claim to the graduates’ seat, citing its victory in the last election. The constituency is currently represented by Arun Lad of NCP. State minister Hasan Mushrif is backing his close associate Pratap alias Bhaiya Mane for the seat. Mushrif has publicly claimed that Arun had persuaded Mane to withdraw from the previous contest by assuring him of support in the subsequent election. He has now challenged Arun to ensure that his son Sharad, whom Mushrif alleges has moved closer to BJP, does not seek the party nomination.The graduates’ constituency is emerging as a crowded field. Former MLC Ranjeetsinha Mohite-Patil of Akluj in Solapur district has also begun preparations for the contest. A key meeting of his supporters has been convened on Sept 24.In Pune division, Arun Lad of NCP won the graduates’ constituency in the previous election, while Congress candidate Jayant Asgaonkar emerged victorious from the teachers’ constituency.Unlike in assembly and Lok Sabha elections, voters in MLC graduates and teachers’ constituencies must register afresh for every election. As voting is conducted through the preferential voting system, aspiring candidates and political parties have already launched intensive enrolment drives to maximise the number of eligible voters before the nomination process concludes.
Article Summary: Election Commission announces biennial elections to Maharashtra Legislative Council from graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies. The voting will be held on Oct 23, with counting and results on Oct 27. The Pune division constituency — covering Pune, Satara, Solapur, Sangli, and Kolhapur districts — will elect one representative each to the legislative council.

Article Title: Cops on Ganpati patrol hit by speeding MUV on Thane-Belapur Road, driver flees
Article Text:
The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday.





NAVI MUMBAI: In a hit-and-run incident on the Thane-Belapur Road, a police constable and a woman assistant sub-inspector (ASI) were injured when a speeding MUV rammed into their motorcycle from behind while they were patrolling during the seventh day of Ganpati immersion.The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday.The injured cops were identified as constable Umesh Patil, 41, who was riding his personal motorcycle, and ASI Rashmin Magar, who was riding pillion.The motorcycle skidded after being hit by the MUV. Patil sustained injuries to his left leg, while Magar suffered bruises to her left elbow, shoulder and left leg.Acting on a complaint filed by Patil, Rabale MIDC police registered an FIR under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Motor Vehicles Act against the MUV driver. Police traced him to his residence in Ghansoli.Devidas Kathale, senior inspector of Rabale MIDC police, said, “As the accused MUV driver's wife is due to deliver in a few days, he will be summoned to the police station later and served with a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.”
Article Summary: The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday. The injured cops were identified as constable Umesh Patil, 41, and ASI Rashmin Magar, who was riding pillion. The motorcycle skidded after being hit by the MUV.

Article Title: Speeding SUV hits bike in Vashi, 3 youths injured; driver traced
Article Text:
Accused driver of SUV Mahindra Thar escaping after accident





NAVI MUMBAI: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday.The incident took place around 1am. The injured youths were initially taken to NMMC Hospital in Vashi and were later referred to Sion Hospital for further treatment.Following the incident, a biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police then traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number.During the investigation, it was learnt that the owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride. Police subsequently traced his mobile tower location to an area near the creek in Sector 12, Vashi, where he was allegedly hiding.He was detained and served a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), following which he was released.
Article Summary: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday. A biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number. The owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride.

Article Title: Quack doctor detained in Maharashtra for practising medicine without registration
Article Text:
A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel police after an inspection (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel taluka police after a complaint was lodged by the medical officer of the Primary Health Centre at Ajivali village in Panvel taluka, following an inspection by health department officials at his illegal clinic in Kasalkhand village on Monday afternoon.The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal and resides in an MHADA building in India Bulls Township, Kon village, Panvel.Gajanan Ghadge, senior inspector of Panvel taluka police, informed that the complaint was lodged by medical officer Dr Sayali Mankar, 33, who inspected Haq's clinic in Kasalkhand village and found that he was an unqualified and unregistered medical practitioner allegedly practising modern medicine by posing as a doctor.He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.Inspector Ghadge said, "We have invoked relevant sections of the Maharashtra Medical Practitioners Act, 1961, against the accused, which prohibit any person from practising medicine in the state unless their name is registered under the relevant statutory provisions and prescribe criminal penalties and fines for those who illegally practise medicine without valid registration. Under the law, the accused was served a notice under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directing him to appear for inquiry when summoned and during the court proceedings. "
Article Summary: The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal. He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.

Article Title: 'Grabbed hand and attempted to disrobe': Cab driver tries to assault woman passenger near Navi Mumbai airport
Article Text:
Police have registered a case and are searching for the accused driver (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver who took the vehicle to a deserted road near Navi Mumbai airport late on Saturday night, police said on Sunday.The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport, police said. The accused allegedly stopped the cab on the pretext of drinking water before moving to the rear seat beside the woman, police said.According to the police, the woman was travelling to Panvel after a friend booked a cab for her following the party."The driver stopped the vehicle on the deserted service road, stepped out briefly, and then re-entered the car, sitting on the rear seat next to the woman. He allegedly grabbed her hand and attempted to disrobe her," said an official of the Navi Mumbai Police.The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.After the incident, the woman contacted her family and went to Panvel Police Station to lodge a complaint.Since the alleged incident took place within the jurisdiction of Navi Mumbai airport police station, Panvel police escorted her to the appropriate police station.Based on her complaint, Navi Mumbai Airport Police registered a case against the accused, identified as Mohammad Afzal Shaikh, under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police have launched a search for Shaikh and are using technical intelligence to trace his whereabouts.Further investigation is underway.(With ANI inputs)(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver. The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport. The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.

Article Title: PM classmate’s battle for land continues despite BJP MLA's exit, no possession yet
Article Text:
Asgar Ali Vora met the PM on Sept 8 and sought his intervention in the land disp­u­te





BHAYANDAR: Asgar Ali Vora, a schoolmate of Prime Minister Narendra Modi , continues to struggle to regain possession of his land after MLA Narendra Mehta’s company announced that it had relinquished the property. However, another developer is allegedly continuing to retain possession of the land.Vora, 81, had purchased around 2,810 sq m of land at Navghar in Bhayandar East in 1989. He has alleged that Swayam Builders and Mehta’s Seven Eleven Constructions took possession of the property in 2011. After pursuing the matter for nearly 15 years, Vora met PM Modi on Sep 8 and complained against Mehta.Following the meeting, Mehta relinquished possession of the land, while the municipal corporation also cancelled the construction permission granted to him.However, the land has allegedly not been handed back to its original owner. Instead, developers Mukesh Parekh and Mervyn Fernandes are allegedly continuing to retain possession of the property. Following a complaint by Shiv Sena, Navghar police have registered a non-cognisable offence against Seven Eleven Constructions, Parekh and Fernandes.
Article Summary: Asgar Ali Vora, 81, had purchased around 2,810 sq m of land at Navghar in Bhayandar East in 1989. He has alleged that Swayam Builders and Mehta’s Seven Eleven Constructions took possession of the property in 2011. After pursuing the matter for nearly 15 years, Vora met PM Modi on Sep 8 and complained.

Article Title: Maharashtra TET paper leak: 2 key accused arrested; 168 buyers on radar
Article Text:
Two key accused in TET paper leak case arrested

How the leak occured





BHIWANDI: Two key accused allegedly linked to 168 prospective buyers of the leaked Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) question paper have been arrested, nearly two months after police busted the racket, with the SIT now probing the wider network and possible transactions.The two — Pune-based govt employee Prakash Misal and Bihar native Ashok Shaw, who was staying in Delhi — were among the remaining prominent accused identified during the probe. Police said Misal was in touch with around 50 people who had shown interest in buying the paper, while Shaw allegedly maintained a list of 118 prospective buyers. The list was recovered from his Delhi residence.Shaw was arrested in Patna, Bihar, while Misal was arrested near Bhiwandi Naka on Sunday after police learnt he was planning to surrender before a court. Both were produced before the Bhiwandi court and remanded in police custody till Sept 23.The SIT has so far verified 18 of the 118 names on Shaw's list and found they were preparing to appear for the TET examination. Verification of the remaining 100 is underway.Police suspect Shaw was directly linked to Solapur-based coaching-class operator Prakash Pawar, who has already been arrested, and was also in contact with alleged mastermind Bijendra Gupta.Investigators are questioning Misal to determine the price at which he allegedly planned to sell the paper and whether any sale took place. Earlier, accused Kapil Dahiya, who had allegedly travelled to Pune to deliver the paper to Misal, told investigators he could not hand it over.Police had busted the racket two days before the scheduled examination, forcing postponement of the TET.DCP Pawan Bansod confirmed the arrests. ACP Sachin Sangle, part of the SIT, told TOI, "Their interrogation will help us establish to whom they intended to sell the paper."Last week, the SIT filed a 3,470-page chargesheet before the Bhiwandi fast-track court against those arrested earlier in the case.With Misal and Shaw's arrests, police said the two remaining prominent accused identified during the investigation have been apprehended. Further arrests will depend on findings from their contacts and financial transactions.
Article Summary: Pune-based govt employee Prakash Misal and Bihar native Ashok Shaw were among the remaining prominent accused identified during the probe. Police said Misal was in touch with around 50 people who had shown interest in buying the paper. Shaw allegedly maintained a list of 118 prospective buyers.

Article Title: Cong neta seeks protection for 'gangrape' survivor, her kin
Article Text:
(Representative image)





THANE: A day after Padgha police registered an FIR against former Kalyan West MLA Narendra Pawar and dismissed policeman Shailesh Patil for allegedly gangraping a 22-year-old married woman at a farmhouse in Bapgaon, Congress group leader in KDMC Kanchan Kulkarni on Friday sought police protection for the survivor and her family.Kulkarni, who accompanied the woman to the police station, claimed the survivor's life was in danger because of the accused's influence. She urged CM Eknath Shinde to intervene and ensure security for her.Meanwhile, Padgha police conducted a spot panchnama at the farmhouse in Bapgaon to collect forensic evidence. Seperate police teams have also been formed to trace Pawar and Patil, who remain absconding. Pawar has denied the charge, calling them false. He has also resigned from all his BJP organisational posts. - Pradeep Gupta
Article Summary: Congress group leader in KDMC Kanchan Kulkarni sought police protection for the survivor and her family. She urged CM Eknath Shinde to intervene and ensure security for her. Padgha police conducted a spot panchnama at the farmhouse in Bapgaon to collect forensic evidence.

Article Title: All-party meet must discuss flagged SIR discrepancies: Supriya
Article Text:
Supriya Sule

Pune:





NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule on Wednesday demanded an all-party meeting to discuss the alleged discrepancies in the SIR exercise.Supriya referred to reports where Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected to some SIR processes. “The opposition raised discrepancies in the SIR but when Election Commission of India (ECI) members have also flagged it, the matter is serious.”Officials said that the two commissioners had flagged decisions related to the deletion of names in various states during the voter roll cleanup and the handling of the voter database.Supriya added that the entire country came together during Operation Sindoor. “In SIR-related issues too, we must rise above politics to safeguard the voting rights of every citizen. Therefore, an all-party meeting should be called for a discussion.”The opposition has demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner of India Gyanesh Kumar over the alleged discrepancies in the SIR process. “It is a national issue directly related to our democratic values and the CEC should take moral responsibility. We will take it up with our INDIA bloc partners,” Supriya added.The SIR process is underway in Maharashtra . Shiv Sena (UBT) Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Raut on Wednesday said, ”Conducting fair elections is the responsibility of ECI but when the CEC does not perform his duties honestly, he should be suspended and legal action taken against him.”Maharashtra Congress chief Harshwardhan Sapkal said the objections raised by Sandhu and Joshi cannot be ignored. “ECI and govt will have to answer with utmost transparency. The electoral rolls are not individual property but part of the country’s democratic process and no compromises should be made,” he added.Congress’s state spokesperson Gopal Tiwari said that in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, MVA won 31 of the 48 Lok Sabha seats in Maharashtra but in the assembly poll a few months later the BJP-led alliance swept the election.“Between the two elections, nearly 41 lakh voters increased in the state. Gyanesh Kumar could not give any logical explanation for the sudden rise in the number of voters. We have been saying there was ECI manipulation and we have been proved right today.”
Article Summary: Supriya Sule demands an all-party meeting to discuss the alleged discrepancies in the SIR exercise. Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected to some SIR processes. The opposition has demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner of India Gyanesh Kumar.

Article Title: Man booked for harassing woman in Coimbatore
Article Text: COIMBATORE: Race Course police in the city have begun investigations after a 30-year-old married woman lodged a complaint alleging that a man, who is her relative, had repeatedly harassed her sexually.In her complaint, the woman said the 36-year-old man had been frequently speaking to her on the phone. Her husband objected to their conversations and warned her against speaking to her relative.However, the relative continued to contact her on the phone. When she had stopped answering his calls, he contacted her using different phone numbers and harassed her, she stated in her complaint.The woman lodged a complaint with Race Course police on Tuesday. Police registered a case under Section 75 of BNS read with Section 4 of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act.
Article Summary: Married woman alleges that a man, who is her relative, had repeatedly harassed her sexually. The woman said the 36-year-old man had been frequently speaking to her on the phone. Her husband objected to their conversations and warned her against speaking to the relative.

Article Title: Two held for possessing prescription tablets for illegal sale in Coimbatore
Article Text: COIMBATORE: RS Puram police have arrested two men on charges of possessing prescription tablets for illegal sale. Police seized 159 tablets from the duo, identified as R Sabarisan Vishwa, 23, of Ramesh Nagar near Achanur in Thanjavur and N Thilagar, 23, of Anna Nagar in Thuraiyur.On Sunday, police received a tip-off about drug pill sales near the DB Road in RS Puram. Following this, they waited before a lodge in RS Puram. During late hours of Sunday, Vishwa and Thilagar came out of the lodge. Upon checking them, police found drug pills in their possession.Police conducted a search in the room the two men were staying in and found more tablets, syringes with needles and Rs 60,000 in cash. Police seized the tablets, syringes, cash and their mobile phones.Further inquiries revealed that Vishwa and Thilagar had procured the contraband from Trichy. They used to visit Coimbatore once a month and stay in the lodge. Since visitors were not allowed inside the lodge, they contacted the buyers over the phone and sold the contraband in places near the lodge.Police registered a case under sections of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The duo were remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: RS Puram police have arrested two men on charges of possessing prescription tablets for illegal sale. Police seized 159 tablets from the duo, identified as R Sabarisan Vishwa, 23, and N Thilagar, 23. The duo were remanded in judicial custody.

Article Title: Explosive materials seized from godown near Chinnalapatti; two booked
Article Text:
Explosive materials seized from godown near Chinnalapatti; two booked

Dindigul:





Dindigul district police raided a godown in Chinnalapatti on Monday and recovered 1,189kg of explosive materials hoarded illegally.Following a tip-off regarding the illegal hoarding of explosive substances, a police team headed by Chinnalapatti police inspector Sathya raided an asbestos-roofed godown situated within the JNS Bakery premises along the Munnilaikottai–Aariyanallur road.According to police, the raid revealed that the property belongs to Sellathurai, also known as Savarimuthu, 64, a resident of South Street in Aariyanallur.About a month ago, the facility had been rented out to Vijayakumar , 39, of Madurai.Police discovered that the warehouse was being used to hoard explosive ingredients and semi-finished products to manufacture paper crackers commonly used for funerals, temple festivals and wedding celebrations, without any valid licence or safety permissions.During the search, personnel seized 1,048kg of unwound paper crackers, 100kg of magic sand, 34kg of fuse wire, 5kg of chemical white powder, and 2kg of gunpowder.Acting on a complaint lodged by Jayalakshmi, village administrative officer of Munnilaikottai village, Chinnalapatti police registered a case against Vijayakumar and Sellathurai.Both accused individuals were absconding, and special teams have launched an active manhunt to track them down and place them under arrest.
Article Summary: Dindigul district police raided a godown in Chinnalapatti on Monday and recovered 1,189kg of explosive materials hoarded illegally. The warehouse was being used to manufacture paper crackers commonly used for funerals, temple festivals and wedding celebrations.

Article Title: Tension in Thoothukudi over PMT leader’s arrest over extortion plaint
Article Text:
Tension in Thoothukudi over PMT leader’s arrest over extortion plaint





Thoothukudi: Tension prevailed in Thoothukudi on Tuesday after police arrested Pasumpon Muthuramalinga Thevar Makkal Paadhugappu Iyakkam (PMT) leader K Esakki Raja following a complaint from a jeweller accusing him of demanding money and issuing threats. Police resorted to a lathicharge to disperse his supporters who held a road blockade outside the court protesting his arrest.K Esakki Raja, 46, a resident of Pasumpon Nagar near Third Mile, was picked up from his house by Thoothukudi South police on Tuesday morning and taken to the police station for questioning. Police said a case was registered against him following a complaint from Velavan Jewellers alleging extortion and criminal intimidation.Police said the dispute has its roots in a three-year-old incident involving Esakkiraj, a functionary of the same party. He had purchased jewellery from Velavan Jewellers in 2023 and subsequently approached a private finance firm to pledge it. He was allegedly informed that the ornaments contained a higher proportion of other metals.Police said K Esakki Raja had intervened in the dispute on behalf of Esakkiraj and allegedly held a kangaroo court.Police also alleged that K Esakki Raja had received Rs 4.22 lakh towards the jewellery dispute and that he demanded another Rs 1 crore from the owner.The management approached police through representatives of the traders' association and lodged a complaint with the district superintendent of police. Police said Esakki Raja was booked for alleged extortion and criminal intimidation after his arrest by Thoothukudi South police on Tuesday.As a large number of PMT supporters gathered outside the police station, the main entrance to the station was closed and armed personnel deployed. When police took Esakki Raja to the medical college hospital for examination, his supporters tried to block the police vehicle and raised slogans demanding his release. Raja was taken back to south police station before being produced before judicial magistrate in Thoothukudi. The magistrate subsequently remanded him in judicial custody till Oct 6.Following the court order, PMT supporters blocked Thoothukudi-Palayamkottai road in front of the court, alleging that police had registered a false case against their leader. After talks failed to yield results, police resorted to lathicharge to restore traffic.While PMT functionaries maintained that the case against Esakki Raja was retaliatory, police said it was based on a complaint accusing him of demanding money and threatening the jewellery establishment.
Article Summary: Pasumpon Muthuramalinga Thevar Makkal Paadhugappu Iyakkam (PMT) leader K Esakki Raja arrested. Police said a case was registered against him following a complaint from Velavan Jewellers alleging extortion and criminal intimidation. Police resorted to a lathicharge to disperse his supporters who held a road blockade outside the court protesting his arrest.

Article Title: Auto driver arrested for threatening, assaulting cops in Yercaud
Article Text:
Representative image





SALEM: The Yercaud police have arrested an autorickshaw driver on charges of assaulting a special sub-inspector (SSI) and threatening to kill the SSI and a woman police constable.The arrested auto driver has been identified as Yuvraj, 22, of Mundagampadi. Yuvraj, who was drunk, obstructed vehicles near a Vinayagar statue on Monday. Head constable D Thavamani, who was regulating traffic, intervened. Yuvraj abused her verbally.SSI Aaron Athirubaraj attempted to defuse the situation. “But Yuvraj tore my shirt, struck me on the chest and threatened to kill me and Thavamani,” the SSI said.Police registered a case against Yuvraj under sections relating to obstructing govt servants, assault and criminal intimidation. He was remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: The arrested auto driver has been identified as Yuvraj, 22, of Mundagampadi. He was remanded in judicial custody. Police registered a case against him under sections relating to obstructing govt servants, assault and criminal intimidation.

Article Title: CMRL case: Keralam govt forms SIT to probe ED findings against Pinarayi Vijayan & kin
Article Text:
Pinarayi Vijayan

Thiruvananthapuram

:





The state govt has constituted a special investigation team (SIT) of Crime Branch to probe information shared by Enforcement Directorate (ED) on CMRL-Exalogic financial transactions involving former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan , his daughter Veena T and son-in-law and former minister P A Mohamed Riyas.Crime Branch ADGP H Venkatesh will supervise SIT, while SP Vikraman will be the investigating officer. The nine-member team comprises three DSPs, three inspectors and other officers. It can be expanded if required during the investigation.The team has been directed to complete the preliminary investigation within 30 days. It will collect details from ED officers who handed over the evidence and documents related to the allegations before deciding on further action. If the team finds evidence to substantiate the charges, it will register an FIR and proceed with a criminal investigation. It could also recommend handing over the probe to an agency such as CBI if the investigation involves transactions or evidence in international jurisdictions, sources said.
Article Summary: The state govt has constituted a special investigation team (SIT) of Crime Branch to probe information shared by Enforcement Directorate. The team has been directed to complete the preliminary investigation within 30 days. It will collect details from ED officers who handed over the evidence and documents related to the allegations before deciding on further action.
